case: A first claimant releasing once, which must not be flagged.
why: The chapter names both columns: the adverse case is a second claimant that re-releases and the benign case is a first claimant releasing once. At the registry layer the benign case is a guard that may be hardened without the pin objecting -- here the allocation timestamp must also be present on the record being claimed, which every legitimate first claim carries. A control that refused this would refuse the ordinary release path, and the adverse count beside it would not be a detection rate.
